extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys) involved in claim drafting and prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on proper form, terminology, specification completeness, and incorporation-by-reference practices for U.S. patent claim drafting and examination, with procedures for examiner actions and required applicant corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim statutory requirements (35 U.S.C. 112(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim in dependent form shall contain a reference to a claim previously set forth and then specify a further limitation of the subject matter claimed. A claim in dependent form shall be construed to incorporate by reference all the limitations of the claim to which it refers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The test is that the dependent claim must include every limitation of the claim from which it depends and specify a further limitation. Omitting or replacing an element of the base claim (e.g., omitting D or replacing D with E when base claim recites A,B,C,D) makes the dependent claim improper. A dependent claim does not lack compliance simply because there is a question as to the significance of the further limitation added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim may cross statutory classes and relate to separate inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that a dependent claim relates to a separate invention requiring a separate search or is in a different statutory class from the claim on which it depends does not, in itself, render it an improper dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a claim to a method of making the product of claim 1 may be a proper dependent claim; a product-by-process dependent claim may be proper only if it includes the limitations of the base claim. Examiner should still treat dependent claim as a combination of base + dependent limitations when comparing to prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of dependent claim to prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent claim is directed to a combination including everything recited in the base claim and what is recited in the dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must compare the combined limitations (as if the dependent claim were presented as one independent claim) with the prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action when dependent claim fails 35 U.S.C. 112(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the dependent claim does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 112(d), the examiner should reject the dependent claim under 35 U.S.C. 112(d) as unpatentable rather than objecting to the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.36 (statutory quotation) and form paragraph 7.36.01 (rejection wording). In form paragraph 7.36.01, insert explanation in bracket 2 explaining what in the claim fails to constitute a further limitation. Form paragraph 7.36 is to be used ONLY ONCE in a given Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence and format of singular and series dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of singular dependent claims is permissible; a claim depending from a dependent claim should not be separated by any claim which does not also depend from said dependent claim. A dependent claim may refer back to any preceding independent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain applicant's sequence in general. During prosecution, renumbering may cause conflicts; check numbering and references carefully when claims are renumbered upon allowance. Use form paragraph 6.18 to advise applicants about series of singular dependent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim terminology and antecedent basis (support in specification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The meaning of every term used in any of the claims should be apparent from the descriptive portion of the specification with clear disclosure as to its import; in mechanical cases identify the part(s) in the drawings to which the term applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid a confusing variety of terms for the same thing. New terms introduced after filing should be supported by appropriate amendment to the specification so there is clear support or antecedent basis (see 37 CFR 1.75(d)(1)). Examiners should ensure late-presented terms find clear support; object the specification using form paragraph 7.44 if it fails to provide proper antecedent basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of specification — written description, enablement, and utility (35 U.S.C. 112)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must include a written description of the invention using such description and details as to enable any person skilled in the art to make and use the invention as of its filing date, and must include at least one specific operative embodiment or example sufficient in scope to justify the scope of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written description must reasonably convey that the applicant was in possession of the claimed invention. Enablement requires disclosure without undue experimentation (complex experimentation that is typical in the art may be allowed). The specification should include a statement identifying a specific and substantial credible utility for the claimed invention. See cited MPEP sections for specialized contexts (e.g., biotech, functional claims, computer programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference — form and allowed scope (37 CFR 1.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation by reference must be set forth in the specification and must (1) express a clear intent to incorporate by reference by using the root words 'incorporat(e)' and 'reference' and (2) clearly identify the referenced patent, application, or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential material may be incorporated only by reference to a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication (37 CFR 1.57(d)). Nonessential material may be incorporated from a broader set (U.S./foreign patents, publications, commonly owned U.S. apps, etc.). An incorporation by hyperlink or other browser executable code is not permitted. Mere reference without the required wording is not an incorporation; examiners will treat ambiguous references as if no incorporation was intended and may require correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of essential material and limits on incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Essential material’ is material necessary to (1) provide the written description/enablement/best mode (35 U.S.C. 112(a)); (2) describe the claimed invention in terms that particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention (35 U.S.C. 112(b)); or (3) describe structure/material/acts corresponding to a claimed means or step (35 U.S.C. 112(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In an application to issue as a U.S. patent, essential material may only be incorporated by reference to a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication. Nonessential (background/state of the art) may be incorporated from a broader list of document types. Examiners should ensure incorporations comply with 37 CFR 1.57(c)-(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and consequences of improper incorporation by reference (37 CFR 1.57(g),(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: An improper incorporation by reference (e.g., incorporation of essential material from an improper source, failure to use required root words, or inadequate identification of the referenced document) is not effective unless corrected within time limits and in accordance with 37 CFR 1.57(g)/(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliant incorporation may be corrected by amendment only if no new matter is introduced; the amendment must include a statement that the material being inserted is the material previously incorporated by reference and that the amendment contains no new matter. Corrections must be made no later than the close of prosecution (37 CFR 1.114(b)) or abandonment of the application. 37 CFR 1.57(h)(1) allows correction where the application as filed clearly conveys an intent to incorporate; 1.57(h)(2) allows correction where the document is sufficiently described to uniquely identify it. Examples: correcting a citation that cannot identify the intended article may constitute new matter and is not authorized; citation by attorney docket alone is insufficient unless it uniquely identifies the document (specify application number if possible). The examiner may require the applicant to supply a copy of incorporated material accompanied by a statement that the copy supplied consists of the same material incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural rules for reference filing and inadvertently omitted material (37 CFR 1.57(a),(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to conditions, an application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) may, by an application data sheet reference to a previously filed application (identified by number, filing date, and authority), constitute the specification and drawings of the new application for purposes of a filing date; if all or a portion of the specification or drawings is inadvertently omitted but is completely contained in a prior-filed application, the omitted portion may be considered incorporated by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on reference filing or omission-correction paths, the applicant must (as applicable) file a copy of the previously filed specification/drawings, provide an English translation if needed, pay required fees/surcharge, and in some cases file a certified copy within specified timeframes (e.g., within later of 4 months from filing or 16 months from previously filed application). If the applicant fails to supply required documents, the application may be treated as never filed or abandoned unless revived under §1.137 and the copy supplied. Any amendment to add omitted material must be made within Office-set time periods and may be subject to petition or fee requirements (e.g., §1.53(e), §1.17(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling of dependent claims when base claim is canceled or rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: If the base claim has been canceled, a claim directly or indirectly dependent thereon should be rejected as incomplete. If the base claim is rejected, the dependent claim should be objected to rather than rejected if it is otherwise allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.43 to state the objection: 'Claim [1] objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.'
